newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mitsui Coal suggests closure of largest Japan mine.
newsitem.headline: Mitsui Coal suggests closure of largest Japan mine.

text.p: Mitsui Coal Mining Co Ltd plans to close the Miike Mine, Japan"s largest coal mine, on March 30, company officials said on Monday.

Mitsui Coal President Minoru Kubo told a news conference that it informed the three labour unions at the mine, located in Fukuoka prefecture on Japan"s southern island of Kyushu, of its decision on Monday.
He said Mitsui Coal"s business has failed to stabilise despite efforts at diversification and cost-cutting.
Kubo said conditions facing the company were likely to become even more severe, forcing the decision to shut the operation.

Negotiations between Mitsui Coal and the labour unions will focus on the re-employment of the 1,207 workers who will lose their jobs with the closure of the mine, as well as other terms such as retirement allowances to be paid by the company.

Miike Mine"s production amounted to about 2.3 million tonnes while sales totalled about 40.6 billion yen in fiscal 1995/96, according to figures provided by the Ministry of International Trade and Industry.
In its heyday in 1970, the mine produced 6.5 million tonnes of coal annually.
Mitsui Coal"s parent company is Mitsui Mining Co Ltd .
